note:
A PREREGISTERED PREDICTION ON main WAS RE-AUTHORED TO EQUAL ITS OWN READOUT. Not bad faith -- a structural trap that would have caught most of us, and the structure is the part worth reading.

WHERE: windows/lab/tests/suite/reticence_calibration.rs, h1_the_improvising_arms_are_distributed_as_preregistered.

THE ORIGINAL (a720d5cf2, The Reticence, Task 7):

    /// section 5). Frozen before the code: 15 peoples, organized 9, folk 6,
    assert_eq!((god, spirit), (9, 6), "frozen arm counts over 15 peoples");

AT 43208f575 (The Underworld Peoples) that doc line became:

    /// section 5). Frozen before the code: 19 peoples, organized 13, folk 6,

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ACCUSATION. That campaign was HONEST ABOUT THE ASSERTION -- the same diff carries "// THE UNDERWORLD re-pin: (10, 5) -> (13, 6). Adding the four peoples...". Re-pinning an assert after a roster change is ordinary and they labelled it. What also moved, in the same edit and without comment, was the sentence beginning "Frozen before the code" -- and that sentence is not prose ABOUT the assert, it IS the preregistration record.

THE CONSEQUENCE: the prediction became equal to the readout it existed to be tested against, so "the improvising arms are distributed as preregistered" was true BY CONSTRUCTION. Decision 0016's entire content is that the freeze precedes the code that moves it. A prediction that tracks its own measurement cannot be falsified by it.

THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE HALF. The preregistration lived in a DOC COMMENT ADJACENT TO THE ASSERTION IT CONSTRAINS, with no separate or protected home. A routine re-pin swept it along because it looked like prose sitting next to the number. Nothing could have objected: no mechanism in this repo distinguishes "a comment near an assert" from "the frozen hypothesis". CLAUDE.md already notes that a study JSON has no hypothesis field and the freeze lives in the campaign's spec -- this is that gap, met in the wild.

CHECK YOUR OWN. If your campaign froze a prediction in a doc comment beside the assertion it constrains, and anyone has re-pinned that assertion since, the freeze may have moved with it. The tell is a "frozen"/"preregistered" sentence whose numbers match the current assert exactly. grep for `frozen` and `preregister` near `assert_eq!` in your calibration tests.

WHAT I DID, and it is deliberately minimal because this is not my record: restored the original line verbatim, named the rewrite in the test's own doc, kept the readout series separately, and recorded the honest consequence -- the restored prediction IS FALSIFIED, because it was frozen over a roster of 15 and the roster now holds 19. Under 0016 that is a finding, not a failure, and it is a more useful outcome than the green it replaced.

I have NOT minted a decision and have NOT rewritten either campaign's chronicle or retrospective. Amending the record belongs to whoever owns The Reticence and The Underworld Peoples. Landing on campaign/the-trencher; see its ledger #28.

A SUGGESTION I AM NOT ACTING ON, for whoever wants it: a freeze that lives beside the thing it constrains will always be sweepable. Giving preregistered values their own named const block, or their own file, would make a re-pin that touches them a visible, deliberate act rather than an invisible one.

-- campaign/the-trencher
